_about: Sculpted column orders and doorway colossi (D-018). Rows in the SITE_SPEC style {v, u, src, tier, note}. Every SHAPE proportion here is tier C: a reconstruction of the type from general knowledge of Achaemenid carving (RECOLLECTION: no measured drawing or scan was available, BLOCKERS B6), fitted to the attested/SITE_SPEC dimensions of each order (height, shaft diameter, flute count, base type, capital type). Unit D = the order's lower shaft diameter (SITE_SPEC); 'fraction of base/capital height' = of the order's baseH/capitalH. Licensed scans or measured drawings would replace these forms (NEEDS #10).

switch.note: technical: camera distance (to a column's axis segment / a colossus centre) beyond which the low-detail mesh is drawn; at 32 m a 10 cm flute spans ~3 px at 1080p and 60 deg, so the V-groove flutes of LOD1 read the same

tessellation.u: segments around / rows [LOD0, LOD1]; crease angles in degrees
tessellation.note: technical: lathe tessellation per LOD and the crease angles above which normals are split (sharp arrises, step edges). LOD0 foot/drum/torus/collar/plain shaft raised in session 4 so the silhouette chord error stays <= 1.5 px at 1 m (tests/detail.test.ts, D-147). D-151: palm 5 per leaf and calyx 3 per rib (were 6 and 4; ring chord error still <= 1.1 px at 1 m) to pay for the protome locks and the rolled volutes within the 25 k column budget

square2.note: square two-stepped plinth under a torus (type IR-PERS, B: Apadana hall bases); step heights C; lower-step width from SITE_SPEC global.r_column_proportions.square2_lower_scale, upper step = the order's baseW

bell.u: fraction of base height (h) / D (r) / fraction of base radius (lip) / profile exponents (radius ∝ (1−t)^flare_pow; rows denser toward the foot)
bell.note: inverted-bell (campaniform) base on a low round foot, torus on top (type IR-PERS, B: porticoes, Gate); bottom radius = half the order's baseW; profile C

bell_leaves.u: count / fraction of bell height / D / fraction of relief / fraction of leaf pitch / fraction of leaf length where the rounded tip begins / fraction of leaf pitch (midrib width; shared by all leaf reliefs)
bell_leaves.note: pendant palm-leaf (petal) band in relief on the bell, tips down, one tier with midribs (motif from photographs of Persepolis bell bases, RECOLLECTION; count, tiers and depth C)

plain.note: low cylindrical drum under a torus (Hadish order, base type C); drum radii from SITE_SPEC global.r_column_proportions.plain_base

torus.u: D / D / count / fraction of flute half-width
torus.note: convex torus under the shaft, carved with horizontal flutes as on Achaemenid bases (RECOLLECTION, C); size C

flutes.u: fraction of flute half-width / D / D
flutes.note: concave flutes meeting in sharp arrises (fluted shafts IR-COL, B; count = SITE_SPEC <building>.flutes); flutes stop short of both ends in rounded terminations, leaving plain bands above the torus and below the capital (RECOLLECTION, C); depth and band heights C. Taper from SITE_SPEC r_column_proportions.shaft_top_ratio

unfluted.note: timber shafts (Treasury) are plaster-sheathed and painted, not fluted (RELIEF-R, B); shafts still under construction (Hall of 100 Columns) are left as unfluted drums because fluting was cut after erection (RECOLLECTION, C)

members.u: surface per member, keyed by the order's material (orders not listed: one material for every member)
members.note: Treasury Hall of 99 Columns: 'wooden plastered and painted shafts on stone bases' (ISAC-PA, B; RELIEF-R: plaster-sheathed timber shafts on stone bases, B). The shafts were painted 'in bright colours' (B) but no colour or pattern was found, so they show bare lime plaster (placeholder, Q-020). The plain bolster-and-abacus capital is the timber bearing block under the beams, left as timber (C: only the shafts are reported plastered)

tessellation.note: technical: samples per flute arc and rows per rounded flute termination

composite_split.note: composite capital bottom to top: drooping-palm bell, upright ribbed calyx, vertical double-volute member, double-bull protome (sequence IR-COL, B; split C). Capital height: SITE_SPEC capital_height where it exists (Apadana 7.8 m), else the same multiple of the shaft diameter (DERIVED, C)

palm.u: D / D / count / D / fraction of member height / leaf length at the rim / profile exponents / leaf half-width, edge softness (fraction of leaf pitch) / midrib height (fraction of relief)
palm.note: inverted bell of drooping palm leaves, tips curling out over the shaft top (RECOLLECTION, C)

calyx.u: D / D / count / D / fraction of member height / profile and rib-section exponents / rib relief at the foot (fraction of the rim relief)
calyx.note: upright calyx with vertical ribs (sepals) flaring to a scalloped rim (RECOLLECTION, C)

bull.u: D / fraction of capital height / D / fraction of the collar height over which it flares from the shaft
bull.note: double-bull capital set on the shaft with a short collar (type IR-PERS, B: Apadana W portico 'double-bull capitals set directly on the fluted shaft'); height 2.2 shaft diameters so the protome keeps the proportions of the composite capital's protome (C)

plain.u: D / fraction of capital height / D
plain.note: Treasury plastered timber posts: plain square bolster under a square abacus of width SITE_SPEC capital_boxes.plain (form not found; C)

frame.note: nominal height of the double-bull protome; width and depth are SITE_SPEC r_column_proportions.capital_boxes.protome (3.4 x 1.1 D); the unit mesh is fitted to each order's box (the beam runs along grid x, C)

body.u: D (x along the beam, bull facing +x, mirrored; y up from the protome base; z across the beam). profile: the side outline (x, y); plan: the top outline (x, z); front: the cross-section outline (z, y); the forepart is their intersection, its arrises rounded by `round`
body.note: two addorsed kneeling bull foreparts joined at the back, a flat saddle between the necks where the main beam sits (type IR-COL, B: 'addorsed foreparts'). D-151: the forepart is blocked out as a carver works a block, from a side, a plan and a front outline, intersected with rounded arrises: planar flanks, a flat chest front for the curl apron and a thick neck (was a union of ellipsoids, which read as a plush toy); a low shoulder muscle on each flank. Outlines RECOLLECTION of Persepolis and Susa bull capitals (C)

head.u: D; head frame: s from the poll toward the muzzle front (poll, muzzle in body x, y), t perpendicular to it in the median plane (up-forward), z across; profile (s, t), plan (s, z), front (z, t) outlines intersected with rounded arrises (`round`); features as [centre] / [a, b, radius] in (s, t, z), mirrored in z
head.note: D-151: a planar bull head held forward, muzzle a little down: flat forehead and cheeks meeting in crisp arrises, a broad squared muzzle with comma-shaped nostrils and the mouth line, large eyes under heavy lids and a brow ridge (was an ellipsoid skull with a round-cone muzzle). Proportions and forms RECOLLECTION of Persepolis capital bulls (the Oriental Institute, Tehran and Metropolitan heads; not read in a source), C

horns.u: D, head frame (s, t, z) as protome.head; horn: path points and radii; ear: root and tip, half-width, half-thickness, depth of the hollow (fraction of the half-thickness); socket_w/socket_d: the joint groove where each inserted piece meets the head
horns.note: The capital bulls' ears and horns were made separately and inserted: a search-engine summary of the Metropolitan Museum's description of its Persepolis bull's head (47.100.83, found reused at Istakhr by Herzfeld): 'the ears and horns had been added separately' (2026-09-23, Q-230; a B-level extract, not a registered source, so the row stays C). In 467 they are in place: each is drawn with a fine joint groove at its root. Horn and ear forms (horns sweeping out, forward and up to a point; leaf-shaped ears with a hollow, set behind and below the horns) RECOLLECTION, C

legs.u: D (outline: x, y in the body frame; z: each leg's centre plane, mirrored; w_upper, w_lower: half-width of the forearm and of the cannon, blended over w_y; knee_c, knee_r: the knee cap; round: arris radius; cleft_x, cleft_w: the cleft between the claws)
legs.note: forelegs folded under the chest (the kneeling pose of the Persepolis capital bulls, RECOLLECTION): a flattened forearm to a squared knee standing forward on the base, the cannon folded back under the brisket, the fetlock and a cloven hoof with a flat sole and a crisp heel (D-151; were chained round cones ending in ball hooves), C. The legs were widened by about a quarter (w_upper 0.098 -> 0.125, w_lower 0.07 -> 0.092 D) after the first previews, where they read as a deer's under the massive chest (C)

curls.u: D (turns: count; groove_w: groove half-width, groove_d: groove depth and bevel: rim width, as fractions of the lock radius / height); apron: the curl field on the chest front and dewlap (body y range, half-width in z, the x beyond which the front is carved); forelock: s range on the head, half-width, and the height above the head axis
curls.note: flat snail locks (D-151): each lock a flat-topped disc with a steep bevelled rim, cut by a spiral groove of 1.5 turns; neighbours coil in opposite senses; staggered rows on the chest front and dewlap (the apron) and a forelock of smaller locks between the horns; the field ends in whole locks (a lock is carved only if its centre lies in the field). Were hemispherical bosses (D-029), which the simplifier left as noisy pits (RECOLLECTION of Achaemenid curl carving, C)

mc.u: D / D / triangles / triangles / degrees / fraction of the cell / simplification weights (error scale; > 1 keeps more triangles)
mc.note: technical: marching-cubes cells (LOD0, LOD1), simplification targets, crease angle, the step of the analytic (SDF-gradient) normals, and the simplification weights: the curl apron and the face keep more triangles, the plain flanks fewer (D-151). LOD1 is generated from the model without the locks and the small features (it is seen beyond lod.switch.column)

member.u: fraction of member width (relief: stems and reeds above the core; scroll_r: roll radius) / fraction of member height (scroll_r_max) / fraction of the roll radius (eye, fill, carve: depth of the channel between the band's turns) / turns (count) / phase (rad) / fraction of the relief (reed_h, eye_h: the eye's rise above the roll's end) / D (core_r, stem_w, reed_pitch) / fraction of the roll radius (reed_inset)
member.note: tall member with double volutes (IR-COL, B). D-151: four rolls run through the member along the beam-crossing axis at the corners of its broad faces, two above curling down and two below curling up, as the volutes of an Ionic capital stood on end; each roll's end carries the spiral (1.75 turns of the rolled band, separated by a rounded channel) round a raised eye; stems join the upper and lower rolls on each broad face, with a reeded panel between them; the narrow faces show the rolls' round sides (form RECOLLECTION of the Persepolis composite capitals, C; Q-235). Cross-section = SITE_SPEC capital_boxes.volute (1.25 x 0.9 D). The D-029 scrolls carved on all four faces were polygonised into jagged facets; rolls and channels are extrusions that simplify smoothly

reference_box.note: the model is authored in metres in this box (= SITE_SPEC gate_nations.r_colossus when written) and scaled to the current r_colossus box

jamb.note: colossus carved from the doorway jamb: the fore-part stands in the round in front of the jamb block (as far as the colossus box projects beyond the wall face), the flank is high relief on the passage face of the block, whose background is cut back by relief_depth inside a back and top frame (Achaemenid/Assyrian gate-colossus type, RECOLLECTION, C)

body.u: m (reference box; x along the body, head +x; y above the plinth; z relative to the body's median plane zc, +z = passage side)
body.note: standing bull body, massive and smoothly modelled (bulls W, human-headed winged bulls E: IR-PERS, B; proportions RECOLLECTION, C); feature_blend (m): the small smooth-union radius joining the features of the head (horns, ears, eyes, lids, nose, brows, moustache, beard, hair) to it, so they keep their edges (D-029)

legs.u: m (reference box; fore_outline: the foreleg's side outline, x from fore_x, y above the plinth; fore_w / hind_w: half-width by height [y, w]; hind_outline in body x; fore_muscle: [dx, y, radius] of the forearm muscle; z of each leg's plane zc ± dz)
legs.note: four legs: the forelegs standing side by side in the round, the hind legs striding in relief (C: the leg count of the Persepolis gate colossi was not verified). D-151: each leg is its side outline (forearm or gaskin, knee or hock, a lean cannon, fetlock, pastern and a cloven hoof with a flat sole) extruded to a width that narrows down the leg, arrises rounded, with the forearm muscle swelling at the front, a tendon groove down the back of each cannon and a tuft of hair (a lock) behind each fetlock: Achaemenid and Assyrian carving of bull legs, RECOLLECTION (were chained round cones on boxes)

bull_head.u: m; the W bulls' head is the capital bull's head (protome.head, protome.horns; D units) scaled by `scale` (m per unit), in its own frame from the poll toward the muzzle
bull_head.note: W doorway bulls (IR-PERS/ISAC, B): the bull head facing out of the doorway (the heads are lost today). D-151: the capital bull's head (protome.head and protome.horns: planar brow and cheeks, a broad squared muzzle, eyes under heavy lids, horns and ears) scaled to the colossus, with a forelock of locks; here the horns are carved with the head (no joint groove: no evidence either way for the gate bulls, C). Form RECOLLECTION, C

human_head.u: m (reference box; x forward out of the doorway, y up, third value = lateral offset from the body plane zc, mirrored); masses as [centre, radii]; front: [x of the brow plane, its backward lean per metre of drop, y where it leans from, rounding]; sides: [half-width of the face planes at the front, their taper per metre toward the back, rounding]; nose: [root, tip, root radius, tip radius, flattening of the bridge]
human_head.note: E doorway: bearded human head (IR-PERS/ISAC, B: 'human-headed winged bulls', bearded, horned tiara); the Persepolis faces are destroyed, so the face is a reconstruction of the type after the royal and guardian heads of the reliefs (RECOLLECTION, C). D-151: a face of planes (a straight brow and nose in one line, flat cheeks), almond eyes under heavy upper lids, a brow ridge, a long straight nose, a moustache sweeping out over the lips, full lips, the rectangular beard, the hair bunched at the nape, bull's ears with earrings (C); was an ellipsoid with features pinned on

crown.u: m / count (horn_r: tube radius at the front and at the back)
crown.note: cylindrical horned tiara (RELIEF-R §2, B for the horned tiara). D-151: three pairs of horns wrapping the cylinder, each thick where the pair meets at the front and tapering round to the back; a band of rosette bosses under a crest of upright ribs (Mesopotamian divine crown convention, RECOLLECTION; details C)

wing.u: m / count (covert_tip: fraction of a row's height taken by the rounded feather tips; prim_step: the step at each primary's lower edge as a fraction of prim_amp; tip_len: extension of the lowest and highest primary beyond x_back)
wing.note: wing (RELIEF-R §2, B: winged) rising from the shoulder along the back to the rear top of the relief field. D-151: rows of coverts in front (overlapping feathers with rounded tips, each row standing over the one below with a crisp step), a split, then long primaries running back along the wing, each with a raised rib and a stepped lower edge where it overlies the one below, their tips stepped at the rear (form RECOLLECTION of Assyrian and Achaemenid wings, C); the D-029 scale lattice read as rows of bubbles

curls.u: m (height, depth, groove_w, groove_d, bevel: fractions of the lock radius; chest_w: half-width of the chest field at its foot and top; chest_side, haunch: outlines (x, y) of the fields on the passage face; pad_h: LOD1 pad height as a fraction of the lock height)
curls.note: flat snail locks (D-151): a flat-topped disc with a steep bevelled rim cut by a spiral groove of 1.5 turns, neighbours coiling in opposite senses, placed on the surface in whole locks: the chest and dewlap (front and passage side), a fringe along the belly line, a patch on the haunch, a tuft behind each fetlock, and on the bull the forelock (RECOLLECTION of Achaemenid and Assyrian colossi, C). Each lock is one template mesh laid on the body (the D-029 bosses were displacements the simplifier left as bubbles)

beard.u: m (bands: [kind, rows of locks | band height in m], top to bottom; strand_d: depth of the grooves between strands; hair: the outline (x, y) of the hair on the passage side; blend: fillet radius of the beard's junction below (on the chest) and at the chin)
beard.note: lamassu beard and hair: the rectangular Achaemenid beard carved in horizontal bands, rows of snail locks alternating with bands of long wavy strands, ending in a row of locks; the hair bunched at the nape in rows of locks; the chest locks stop chest_gap below the beard, the beard standing off the smooth chest band in a crisp step (convention of Persepolis royal and guardian heads, RECOLLECTION, C; D-029, D-151)

mc.u: m / m / triangles / triangles / degrees / fraction of the cell / triangles per lock / simplification weights
mc.note: technical: marching-cubes cells (LOD0 0.014 m so the grooves span more than one cell), budgets (the locks are template meshes counted in lod0), crease angle, analytic-normal step, simplification weights (the face and the wing keep more triangles, the flat jamb faces fewer; D-151)
